checked: Treaty text (Oklahoma State University): Detroit, November 17, 1807, 7 Stat. 105, proclaimed January 27, 1808; Articles 2 to 6 match the promises ($10,000, $2,400 annuity at Detroit, commutation, two blacksmiths for ten years, hunting and fishing, the reserved tracts).

ICC interlocutory order of May 11, 1978 (OSU id 2515): values on January 27, 1808 of $600,000, $2,300,000 and $3,500,000; consideration $57,717.32 paid collectively; unconscionable; net $579,308.00, $2,292,000.00 and $3,479,308.00 less gratuitous offsets. All quoted.

Opinion of the same day (OSU id 1932): tract acreages 469,116, 1,843,779 and 3,298,637, total 5,611,532 stated by the Commission; title decision 30 Ind. Cl. Comm. 388 (1973), aff'd 207 Ct. Cl. 960 (1975).

Final awards of June 22, 1978 (OSU ids 1936 and 1725): $2,292,000.00 Docket 29-E and $579,308.00 Docket 133-B, entered on motion after contested valuation, not settlements; kind claims-commission is right.
1973 findings (OSU id 2519): the Wyandot claims in Docket 140 not supported by any evidence and dismissed; correctly kept out of breaches.
